항목.프롬프트: Wide illustrated story panel for a children's Bible game, one single full-bleed scene with no border and no frame: at the open wooden gate of the small mud-brick town of Ziklag. In the center, David, a ruddy Israelite man of about twenty-eight with tousled reddish-brown hair, bright eyes, a handsome kind face and a short reddish-brown beard, wearing a plain light-brown wool tunic with a leather belt, a short sword at his side and sandals, stands in the gateway and welcomes newcomers with both arms open and a big smile. On the far left, well apart from everyone, a Benjamite archer with black hair and a short black beard in a dark green tunic holds a curved wooden bow in his left hand and draws the bowstring back to his cheek with his right hand, aiming up at the sky. On the far right, well apart from everyone, a second Benjamite warrior with black hair and a short black beard in a dark green tunic swings a leather sling above his head with his right hand and holds a small leather pouch of stones at his hip with his left hand. Far behind them more warriors walk up the dusty road, small. Bright sunny day. All houses are one-story mud-brick houses with flat earthen rooftops and low parapets; no sloped roofs, no roof tiles, no red tiles. Hands are drawn simply and clearly, each hand with four fingers and a thumb, and no hand overlaps another person. Every face is clear and well drawn with distinct eyes, nose and mouth. Every person has exactly two arms, two hands, two legs and two feet.
